newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Gordon sworn in as Bermuda's first woman premier.
newsitem.headline: Gordon sworn in as Bermuda's first woman premier.

text.p: Pamela Gordon was sworn in as Bermuda's sixth and first woman premier in a brief ceremony on Thursday, becoming the youngest person to hold the office.

After applause from senior members of the ruling United Bermuda Party, Gordon, 41, said, "If anyone doubted where the United Bermuda Party is going, they just have to walk in this room this morning. The support base behind me is phenomenal and I want to acknowledge the fact that the premier is only as good as the people behind her."

The first person to step forward and congratulate the new premier was David Saul, her predecessor, who shook the UBP last week by announcing that he would resign after less than two years in the office.
The UBP has ruled Bermuda for the past 30 years and needed a candidate for premier who could face the challenge of the general election, due to be held within 18 months.

Political observers said Gordon, the daughter of one of the fathers of modern Bermuda politics, was the only credible choice from among the 21 UBP members of parliament, although she has been a member for less than four years.
She was the only member of the ruling party nominated to replace Saul by the Monday deadline.

The party was hurt by a divisive referendum on independence in August 1995 in which voters opted overwhelmingly to remain a British colony, and a continuing debate over whether a former premier, Sir John Swan, should be permitted to open McDonald's restaurants on the conservative, strictly zoned island.

A virtually unchanged Cabinet also was sworn in at Government House on Thursday. The only new face was John Irving Pearman, a veteran UBP politician who replaced the new premier as Minister of the Environment.

Gordon's father, Trinidad-born physician E.F. Gordon, was a controversial member of parliament in the 1940s and 1950s who pressed the island's white power structure to give way to black political involvement.
Bermuda has been a British colony for more than 380 years.
